page: Amazon Web Services m5d.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and built on the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz, providing 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity totals 256.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance integrates 2400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps without bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate solid multi-core and memory subsystem capabilities alongside modest single-thread metrics. In PassMark, the instance achieved a multi-threaded CPU score of 44,078.3 and delivered top-tier results in extended instructions (52,991.8) and database operations (21,664.66). Uncached memory bandwidth scored in the top 25%, with 189.99 GB/sec read and 91.19 GB/sec write. In contrast, single-thread performance trails modern offerings, as indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1055.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1284.68. Similarly, LLM text generation throughput sits in the lower percentiles.

From an architectural tradeoff perspective, the m5d.16xlarge trades per-core single-threaded speed for parallel resource density, broad memory throughput, and low-latency ephemeral NVMe capacity. The high local storage volume combined with substantial DDR4 bandwidth provides efficient qualitative value for scratch-heavy operations without relying purely on network-attached storage. It is well matched for distributed database clusters, in-memory caching systems, batch processing, static web serving fleets, and data manipulation pipelines requiring dedicated high-core capacity.
description: Amazon Web Services m5d.16xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based virtual instance featuring 64 vCPUs (32 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor at 3.1 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, the configuration pairs 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory with 2400 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage and 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks highlight strong uncached memory bandwidth (189.99 GB/sec read and 91.19 GB/sec write) and high database operation metrics, while single-threaded tasks and sequential decompression reflect lower relative performance. Offering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory distribution coupled with rapid local NVMe IOPS, the m5d.16xlarge provides a balanced hardware profile suitable for relational databases, Redis caching layers, Clang software builds, and multi-threaded data transformation jobs.
